html:
SMTO-JOB-0006 — SMTO can't control that job from this task

GUID: e942e223-1ac2-4636-8409-806dc9ff5994
Slug: job-reference-scope-invalid
Domain: JOB · Subsystem: job

What happened

  • SMTO tried to manage a job it can't confirm belongs to this task, or one started by an earlier attempt that it can only look at. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task continue. SMTO usually picks a different next step on its own. Nothing was changed, and SMTO can still look at the job even though it can't control it.
  2. If you want to know what that job did, ask SMTO in the conversation to show its status and latest output. Looking at a job is allowed even when stopping or changing it isn't.
  3. If SMTO keeps referring to a job you don't recognize, ask it to check which jobs this task actually started. The job it named may belong to another task or may not exist.

What success looks like

  • The task moves on, and SMTO only acts on jobs this task started.

If it still fails

  • If the task stops, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to take over a job that belongs to a different task.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The job reference is unknown or out of scope for this run, or is an inherited observation used for a control other than inspect, reconcile or logs.

What this means

  • Job lookup/settlement cannot prove exact run/job/result ownership, or an inherited job observation is used for a control other than inspect, reconcile or logs. Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.

Why this can happen

  • Job lookup/settlement cannot prove exact run/job/result ownership, or an inherited job observation is used for a control other than inspect, reconcile or logs.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare job ID, owning run, receipt operation identity and whether the job is inherited evidence.

How to fix it

  • RunStore.job/settle_job raise unknown_or_out_of_scope_job when the job_id is not owned by this run; _inspect_job allows only inspect, reconcile and logs for inherited_jobs; manage_tasks rejects a task job_id that job_lookup cannot resolve. Use the job_id from this run's own receipts; inherited observations do not grant control or cancellation authority.
  • Inspect the job through its owning task and use only the controls permitted for the current attempt. Inherited evidence does not grant mutation or cancellation authority.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Only supported observations or controls within actual job ownership are admitted.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
